text: Attach a returns label to every boundary fixture carrying its measured byte budget and offending tail, so a cap failure goes straight back to its fixture owner instead of reopening unrelated checks.
rationale: Returns preserve the raw failure while localizing repair.

text: Materialize a fixture only at the instant its owning command is dispatched, then scrap it after the transcript is captured to prevent stale shared state from crossing workers.
rationale: Just-in-time inventory removes drift without changing the required command.

text: Cross-dock worker evidence through one handoff envelope: route by owner, pass raw exits unchanged, and let the independent checker receive the parcel without a parent’s second interpretation.
rationale: Cross-docking cuts interpretive rework while keeping acceptance independent.

text: Pack the final UTF-8 truncation and gitstatus-slice assertions as last-mile delivery checks at the artifact boundary, rather than repeating them in each upstream repair.
rationale: Last-mile ownership puts boundary invariants beside the delivered bytes.

text: When repairs share a command shape, ship one batched setup parcel with separate fixture labels and raw transcripts for each case.
rationale: Batching amortizes setup while retaining case-level proof.

text: Return a rejected patch with a stamped delta of line, byte count, exit code, and owner, rebuilding only that damaged parcel while completed routes remain closed.
rationale: A precise return route avoids whole-run replay without hiding failure evidence.
